Hanzi Writer 3.7.3: https://github.com/chanind/hanzi-writer (MIT).
Hanzi Writer Data 2.0.1: https://github.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data.
Stroke data is derived from Make Me a Hanzi (https://github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi), based on Arphic fonts; see hanzi-data-ARPHICPL.TXT and hanzi-data-README.md for licenses and attribution.

HSK 2.0 vocabulary coverage (levels 1–4): Complete HSK Vocabulary by drkameleon, https://github.com/drkameleon/complete-hsk-vocabulary (MIT; see hsk-vocabulary-LICENSE).

Vietnamese dictionary definitions and additional pronunciation/context data in writing-catalog.json are adapted from CVDICT by Phong Phan, https://github.com/ph0ngp/CVDICT, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. CVDICT is derived from CC-CEDICT / Paul Andrew Denisowski and contributors. The adapted dictionary dataset writing-catalog.json is distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0. Changes: simplified single-character selection for HSK1–4, editorial definitions, tone-mark conversion, HSK grading, stroke counts, and pronunciation contexts. See CVDICT-README.md for source notes. Dictionary meanings are intended as learning aids and may need teacher review in context.

Single-syllable Mandarin recordings: David A. V. Infield, mp3-chinese-pinyin-sound, https://github.com/davinfifield/mp3-chinese-pinyin-sound (Unlicense / public domain; see pinyin-audio-LICENSE). Selected syllables were resampled to mono MP3 and packed with byte offsets. Where no neutral-tone recording exists, a shorter mid-pitch neutral syllable is derived from the corresponding recorded syllable. Three missing tonal recordings use device Mandarin synthesis of a single homophonic character (标 / 翔 / 休); no vocabulary phrases are spoken.

Recording update: packed syllables were loudness-normalized using a -14 LUFS target and -1 dBTP true-peak limit, then re-encoded as mono 32 kbps MP3.
